How to Make a Clean Signature Image for Online Forms

By Kamlesh Mohabe, Software Engineer · Published 2026-10-04

How to photograph or scan a signature so it stays readable at 10–20 KB: paper, pen, light, cropping, and what to do when the file is too small or too large.

Why signatures are special

A signature is mostly white paper with thin dark lines. That makes it compress very well, which is good when a form asks for a small file. But thin lines are also easy to damage if you compress too hard. The aim is a crisp, dark line on a clean white background.

Question: What paper and pen should I use?

Use plain white paper without lines or patterns, and a black or dark blue pen with a medium tip. Very thin pens can disappear at small sizes. Very thick markers can blur the shape. Sign inside a box you drew with a ruler so the image has a clear boundary, and so you leave room around the signature.

Question: How do I photograph it?

Put the paper on a flat surface near a window, with soft daylight and no shadow of your hand or phone across it. Hold the phone directly above the paper, parallel to it, so that the lines are not distorted. Use the highest-quality camera setting, and avoid the flash, which creates a bright patch.

Question: How should I crop?

Crop to the signature with a small, even margin of white around it. Too tight, and the signature is cut or looks cramped. Too loose, and the signature becomes small and faint inside a large empty picture. If the form asks for particular dimensions, match the shape as closely as you can before compressing.

Question: What size should the file be?

Read the range on the form. Many forms use a range such as 10–20 KB, but others differ. Use the exam range presets on our government exam page, or type a custom target. The presets aim a little below the maximum so the file stays inside the limit under either way of counting kilobytes.

Question: Mine is too small. Is that a problem?

It can be, if the form has a minimum. A very clean signature on a small crop may be only a few KB. Take a larger, sharper photo, crop with a little more margin, and try again. The tool warns you when the result is below the minimum for the range you chose.

Question: Mine is too large. What now?

Check that the paper is clean, because shadows and texture add detail that costs bytes. Reduce the maximum width in Advanced settings. Use JPEG output. Avoid screenshots of screenshots.

Keep your signature consistent

Some exams compare your uploaded signature with the one you give later. Use your normal signature and practise the version you upload.

Quick checklist before you upload

White paper, dark pen, even daylight, no shadow, phone held straight above the page. Crop with a small margin, pick the size range from your form, compress, and look at the result at full size. The lines should be dark and continuous, with no white gaps. Confirm the size is inside the range, including the minimum. Save the file with the name the form asks for and keep the original photograph.
